coverage_gaps: Layer 1B evidence is strongest for US-listed backend/test and semiconductor software names; non-US suppliers in Taiwan, Japan, Korea, and Europe need primary-source filings and local exchange verification.
Market-cap buckets are approximate and should be refreshed with current market data before Layer 2 promotion, especially for non-US listings and recent IPO/relisting cases.

Optical interconnect universe needs deeper primary-source checks for revenue exposure by layer: transceiver assembly, lasers, InP substrates, silicon photonics foundry, epitaxy capacity, and epitaxy tools.

Power/cooling and electrical infrastructure candidates remain underdeveloped; the current universe includes reference anchors and hypotheses but needs a systematic search for smaller component suppliers, liquid-cooling vendors, power modules, switchgear, transformers, and thermal subsystems.
Cybersecurity, identity, observability, automation, and data-governance candidates remain low-confidence hypotheses until product-level and revenue-level AI exposure is verified.
Customer concentration and single-customer dependency are not yet mapped; this is critical for optical, EMS, OSAT, and specialty semiconductor suppliers.
Analyst-coverage, liquidity, valuation, and ownership screens were not fully applied in Layer 1C and should be added before any company advances to a high-conviction research list.

Several reference leaders were retained to map supply-chain context, but Layer 2 should prevent them from crowding out smaller suppliers unless their exposure is unusually pure or necessary for benchmarking.

memory_update.text: Technology theme should remain decomposed around AI compute buildout, cloud infrastructure, semiconductors, optical interconnect, power/cooling, security, and automation rather than around a single mega-cap ticker.
Highest-priority underfollowed node is HBM-adjacent backend test and advanced packaging: probe cards, inspection/metrology, handlers, OSAT overflow, and semiconductor data orchestration.

Optical interconnect should be tracked down-stack into lasers, InP substrates, silicon photonics foundry, qualified epitaxy capacity, and epitaxy tools rather than only transceiver or networking leaders.

Semiconductor manufacturing orchestration software is a non-obvious data-layer node linking fabless, foundry, OSAT, test, and equipment workflows; PDF Solutions is the current cleanest Layer 1 candidate.

Data-center power, cooling, water, electrical distribution, cabling, and component suppliers remain relevant second-order AI infrastructure nodes but need a broader candidate search beyond Vertiv and Eaton.
AI cybersecurity, identity, observability, and automation software should remain in the funnel as low-confidence hypotheses requiring product-level and revenue-level evidence.

Layer 2 must collect primary-source filings, investor presentations, transcripts, current market caps, liquidity, analyst coverage, customer concentration, and valuation checks before promoting any Layer 1C candidate.

Non-US listings are essential for this theme because several chokepoint suppliers sit in Taiwan, Japan, Korea, and Europe; dashboard symbol normalization and ADR/local-listing deduplication are required.

summary: Merged Layer 1 universe for the broad Technology theme using Serenity funnel logic: start from AI compute buildout, then map one- and two-step-removed chokepoints across HBM/backend packaging, semiconductor test, optical interconnect, compound-semiconductor substrates/tools, semiconductor manufacturing data orchestration, data-center power/cooling, and second-order enterprise software/security. The initial universe intentionally balances reference leaders with underfollowed or messy-label suppliers. Highest Serenity relevance is currently in HBM-adjacent backend/test, optical/compound-semiconductor supply chain, and semiconductor workflow data orchestration. Several names remain hypotheses because candidate-level primary-source revenue exposure still needs verification.
